repaired.name: Scenario
repaired.script:
fired := false
if (fired == true) {
wait until(not (all(#PresenceSensor).presenceSensor_presence == true))
fired = false
}
wait until(all(#PresenceSensor).presenceSensor_presence == true)
all(#ColorControl).colorControl_setColor("purple")
fired = true

diagnosis.summary: The IR specifies a rising-edge wait on PresenceSensor.Presence. At t=0, Hallway_PresenceSensor_2 is already true (F1), so the rising edge has fired immediately. The IR executes the body at t=0. The candidate's guard `if (triggered == true)` is false initially, causing it to block on the wait until the condition becomes false (line 3), missing the immediate action required by the rising edge at t=0.
diagnosis.change_summary: Replaced the periodic polling pattern with the standard rising-edge rearming pattern: initialize `fired := false`, check if `fired` is true to block until the condition drops, then block until the condition rises, execute the body, and set `fired = true`. This ensures the body executes immediately if the condition is already true at start.
